regional.syndrome: Febrile illness with prominent respiratory symptoms, meningitis and meningoencephalitis; unlike La Crosse virus, it affects adults disproportionately.
regional.headline: California-serogroup virus causing febrile and neuroinvasive disease mainly in adults in North America; Inkoo virus is its Eurasian counterpart.
regional.geography: United States and Canada; Inkoo virus across northern Europe and Russia.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Abrupt febrile illness ('Oropouche fever') with severe headache, myalgia, arthralgia, chills, photophobia and nausea; frequently relapsing after a few days of apparent recovery. Aseptic meningitis and meningoencephalitis occur. Vertical transmission with fetal loss and congenital anomalies reported during the 2024 expansion, as well as rare fatalities.
regional.headline: The most important human pathogen of the Simbu serogroup and, after dengue, one of the most frequent arboviral febrile illnesses in the Amazon basin. Major expansion across the Americas from 2023–2024.
regional.prevention: Midge control is difficult (C. paraensis is tiny and bites outdoors by day); fine-mesh screening, repellents, reduction of peridomestic breeding (decaying banana/cacao debris).
regional.geography: Amazon basin — Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia, Panama, Trinidad; marked 2024 expansion including Cuba and travel-associated cases exported to Europe and North America.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Often biphasic — a febrile viraemic phase, a symptom-free interval, then meningitis, meningoencephalitis or meningoencephalomyelitis. Mortality ~1–2% for the European subtype with frequent long-term sequelae; the Far Eastern subtype is more severe.
regional.headline: Principal cause of tick-borne encephalitis in Europe; vaccine-preventable.
regional.prevention: Inactivated vaccines (FSME-IMMUN, Encepur) are highly effective; tick checks, pasteurisation of milk.
regional.geography: Central, eastern and northern Europe, expanding northwards and to higher altitudes.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fever, severe headache, abdominal and back pain, transient myopia, proteinuria and acute kidney injury; thrombocytopenia is typical. Case fatality below 0.5%, but hospitalisation is often required.
regional.headline: Cause of nephropathia epidemica, the mild form of HFRS and the most common hantavirus disease in Europe.
regional.prevention: Rodent exclusion from dwellings; precautions when cleaning sheds and cabins. No vaccine in Europe.
regional.geography: Fennoscandia, the Baltic states, central and western Europe, Russia.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Usutu virus. Human neuroinvasive cases and blood-donor seropositivity in Europe.
regional.geography: Usutu virus. Human neuroinvasive cases and blood-donor seropositivity in Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
